summary: High Society is a fast, brutal Knizia bidding game where players spend cash cards to win luxury items, except the player with the least money left at the end is disqualified from winning entirely. It plays in about 20 minutes but demands sharp psychological reads on when to bid, when to fold, and when to bail using the one escape card.
praised: quick, tense, and easy to teach
clever last-place-elimination twist forces careful spending
great psychological bluffing and bidding tension
small box, big impact for filler slot
criticised: can feel purely mathematical/dry to some
luck of card order affects available bidding options
one bad early bid can tank a player's whole game

interaction.detail: There is no board; a single common deck of cards is revealed one at a time and every player bids on it with their own money cards, so winning a card comes entirely at the expense of the other bidders' chance at it and can drain the cash they need at game end. There is no direct attack on an opponent's holdings and no negotiation, just competitive bidding on shared cards.

subsystems: auction bidding for prestige and liability cards
scoring.how_you_win: You bid your limited cash to win valuable cards and avoid costly ones; once the last of the four special cards is drawn the game ends, the player left with the least money is disqualified, and among the rest the highest card total wins.
